label: header
text: CHINA MAIL, JUNE 25, 1925.

label: text
text: LATEST FROM SHAMEEN: -- According to the Hengkong Naval authorities meetings have taken place between the representatives of the Concessions and the Canton Government and as a result of these, the Canton Government has given a guarantee that no further attacks will be made against Shameen pending the outcome of negotiations that are now proceeding. Canton is quiet.

label: text
text:
SWATOW STRIKE: -- Advices from Swatow state that the strike is now in full swing there.
Unrost is reported from Amoy and Hainan.

label: text
text: LOCAL DOCKS:-- Workmen employed by local docks left today. Some of them stated that they would be away for the Dragon Festival only and would be back tomorrow.

label: text
text: MONEY CHANGERS¹ SQUEEZE:--- The Government should note that money changers in Hongkong are taking advantage of the situation to exact exorbitant rates, some demanding, instead the usual two cents, as much as 16 or even 25 cents for $5 in small change.

label: text
text: FOOD PRICES: - Rice retailers are also exploiting the public necessity. They advance their prices whilst their customer is in the shop, as much as they think he will stand.

label: paragraph_title
text: AMBULANCE BRIGADE (MEN).

label: text
text: CHINESE TRADE: - It has been stated that some of the Chinese wholesale traders are interviewing the exchange banks with regard to the question of taking up drafts during the crisis as they are unable to withdraw cash deposited with native bankers.

label: text
text: All Members and former Members of the Ambulance Brigade, and all who are willing to join as temporary Members of the Brigade for Ambulance Service, are requested to communicate as early as possible with Mr. E. Ralphs, at the Education Offices (P. & O. Building) or to meet him there at 5 p.m. tomorrow, Friday, the 26th inst. Members should attend in uniform or with badges, if possible.

label: text
text: THE GREAT NORTHERN TELEGRAPH COMPANY? LIMITED, OF DENMARK? HONGKONG STATION.

label: text
text: The public is hereby notified that our messongers having refused work, delay can be expected in the delivery of telegrams.

label: text
text: To accelerate delivery the public are kindly requested to apply at our office for any tolegrams they may be expecting.

label: text
text: Hongkong, 25th June, 1925.

label: text
text: LANE, CRAWFORD, LTD. regret that owing to CAFE WISEMAN'S office staff having gone out on strike, they are obliged to ask for cash in this department. All other departments as usual. Prices as usual.

label: paragraph_title
text: HONGKONG STOCK EXCHANGE.

label: text
text: Notice is given that the Hongkong Stock Exchange is closed until further noticed and that the June Settlement is postponed till Tuesday, July 7th, 1925.

label: paragraph_title
text:
A. Nissim,
Secretary.

label: text
text:
HONGKONG SHAREBROKERS' ASSOCIATION.
Notice is given that the Hongkong Sharebrokers' Association is closed until further notice and that the June Settlement is postponed till Tuesday, July 7th, 1925.

label: paragraph_title
text:
J. W. Kow,
Secretary.

label: text
text: An Emergency having been declared today by His Excellency the Governor, all persons wishing to offer their services in the public interest are requested to report themselves to the office of the Labour Controller, City Hall.

label: text
text: Persons who have already registered at Police Headquarters for essential services need not so reprpt: their names are already on record.

label: text
text: Companies or persons requiring essential labour should make written application to the Controller of Labour.

label: text
text: (Sgd.) G. M. Young,

label: paragraph_title
text: NOTICE.

label: text
text: City Hall, Juno 22, 1925.

label: text
text: All Chinese British subjects are requested to report themselves at the City Hall, between the hours of 10 a.m. and 6 p.m. on any day before Saturday, the 27th instant.

label: paragraph_title
text: S. W. T'BO,

label: text
text: Assistant:Hongkong, 25th June, 1925.

label: text
text: The s.s. Mirzapore sails for Singapore and usual India ports at noon on Thursday, July 2, 1925. Through bills of lading to usual Continental ports and London will be issued.

label: text
text: LOCAL AND GENERAL.

label: text
text: London, June 24: -- Suzanne Longlen, wearing an orange bandeau, played brilliant tonnis at Wimbledon. Partnered by Miss Ryan, who outclassed Mrs. Lycett and Miss Colyer. - Router.

label: text
text: The weather forecast for tomorrow is as follows: - Easterly winds, moderate, fair to showery.

label: text
text: According to a Router cable the United States Treasury is planning taxation relief to the extent of $300,000,000.

label: text
text: Thero was a clean bill of health for Hongkong yesterday.
